title: Reactor proportional setpoint weighting
equipment: Jacketed stirred reactor, product-temperature transmitter, and jacket heating valve
physicalPurpose: Reduce setpoint overshoot without weakening the already acceptable cold-feed disturbance rejection of the reactor PI loop.
principalTechnique: Two-degree-of-freedom proportional setpoint weight with true-error integral action
objective: Configure and compare proportional setpoint weights of one, one-half, and zero on the same jacketed-reactor PI loop; predict each controller's immediate valve response to a setpoint step; and use retained servo and regulatory evidence to select the largest weight that satisfies the setpoint-overshoot requirement without changing the fixed-setpoint disturbance path.

simplifications: The well-mixed reactor and jacket are represented by one local thermal state.
The five-degree output-balance event is the equivalent thermal effect of colder feed.
Reaction heat, composition dynamics, fouling, valve nonlinearity and independent trips are omitted.

baseline.limitation: Full proportional setpoint response produces 1.049 degC overshoot and fails the declared 1.0 degC servo requirement despite acceptable regulatory recovery.

change.decision: Change only proportional setpoint weight, restart after each initialization-only setting change, retain true-error integral action, and repeat both objective tests from fresh identical initial states.

disturbances: Each fixed-80 degC regulatory run applies the same cold-feed-equivalent event at 60.0 s

acceptance.window: 5.1 through 55.0 s for every servo run
mean from 110.1 through 120.0 s after qualified recovery

abortPredicates: SP, PV, MV or b is nonfinite
PV or MV leaves its hard limit
Gains, true-error integral behavior, plant, initial state, limits, timing or seed differ between runs
safety.restorationMode: At 55.1 s for servo or 120.1 s for regulatory, select Manual with a distinct zero-percent request and retain every rate-constrained update until the applied valve reaches zero
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The setpoint and cold-feed-equivalent experiments are simulation evidence and do not authorise physical reactor actions.

video.viewerOutcome: Derive proportional setpoint weighting and prove that it reduces servo overshoot without weakening true-error integral or fixed-SP load rejection.
requiredVisibleEvidence: weighted P and true-error I equations

learning.context: Lesson 11's unchanged b=1 PI rejects the load acceptably but fails the 1.0 degC servo-overshoot requirement, so retuning would risk sacrificing a working regulatory path.
learning.reason: Weighting only the proportional setpoint contribution can reduce reference aggressiveness while preserving proportional feedback to PV and true-error integral action.
theory: The weighted proportional increment is Kp times b times the SP change minus the PV change, while the integral increment always uses the true error SP minus PV.
b=1 gives full proportional setpoint response, b=0 removes proportional response to SP changes, and intermediate b trades servo speed and overshoot.
With fixed SP, the weighted SP-change term is zero, so changing b does not alter the nominal disturbance path.
Setpoint weighting is dimensionless and is not a measurement filter; it cannot solve sensor-noise transmission.
learning.workedPrediction: For Kp 8 and a 5 degC SP step, the immediate proportional setpoint contributions are 40 percent at b=1, 20 percent at b=0.5 and 0 percent at b=0; a 1 degC PV increase still contributes -8 percent for every b.
practicalPreparation: Recall the Lesson 11 requirements and inspect the same reactor, signals, disturbance, operating point, limits and safe state.
Calculate all three proportional contributions, verify true-error integration and approve six fresh runs with identical gains, plant, timing, events, limits and seed.
learning.baseline: At b=1, establish 80 degC for 5 s, step to 85 degC and reproduce 1.049 degC overshoot; retain the separate fixed-SP load run.
learning.change: Repeat both fresh experiments at b=0.5 and b=0, changing only proportional setpoint weight.
learning.comparison: Compare 1.049, 0.882 and 0.807 degC servo overshoot, then overlay the three regulatory PV/MV traces and measure their maximum numerical difference.
learning.validation: Determine numerical validity first, then apply the common 1.0 degC servo-overshoot requirement with 0.01 degC tolerance, qualify regulatory recovery before calculating mean absolute error from 110.1 through 120.0 s, prove aligned PV and applied-MV disagreement no greater than 1e-10, and select the largest eligible weight only from complete equivalent evidence.
learning.explanation: Explain why the proportional SP kick changes, why feedback to PV and true-error integral do not, and why b=0.5 is the largest tested weight that satisfies the servo requirement without changing load rejection.
learning.transfer: For another loop with good regulatory but aggressive servo behavior, calculate candidate weighted P steps, compare equivalent fresh servo and load runs, and choose the largest b that meets servo requirements while preserving the regulatory trace.
